column3: According to Will Larson, in his model of an engineering organization's seniority mix, if promotion rates at a level exceed the rate of hiring at that level plus the backfill from the level below, the proportion of engineers at that level grows over time. He writes that a company that does little hiring and has high retention cannot afford to promote frequently, so promotion into senior roles becomes financially restrained, even if the policy is explained by some other mechanism. He adds that many companies use a "career level" policy to mark the level where promotions generally stop, and concludes that the rationale is likely a financial constraint.
